turns.t: Doctor, I'm so worried. I've not wanted any food and I've lost weight, and I don't know what's happening to me.
Come and sit down, Mr Okonkwo. We'll look into it together. Who's with you today?
I'm Dee, I'm his carer. I come in each morning and evening. I brought him because I'm worried too.
Thank you, Dee, that's helpful. Mr Okonkwo, let me check I have it right. You're not wanting food and you've lost weight.
Yes. Is it serious? Tell me the truth.
I'll tell you everything as I learn it. First, how long has the appetite been poor?
About three weeks. He leaves nearly the whole plate, and he used to love his stew.
Three weeks, yes, it sounds right. Though it feels longer.
And the weight. When did you first notice that?
Oh, I couldn't tell you. My trousers were loose one day and I couldn't say when it began.
That's all right. Dee, have you noticed a change?
His belt's gone in two holes, but I only started keeping an eye on it recently, so I can't give a date either.
So the weight loss has crept up and you can't pin down when. Fair enough.
And I'm very tired, doctor. Very tired, all day, even after sleeping.
Very tired all day. Noted. Any vomiting?
No vomiting.
And does it hurt when you swallow food?
No, no, swallowing's fine. I just don't fancy anything.
Okay, that's helpful. Now, what tablets do you take?
The one for my heart. Dee, what's it called?
Bisoprolol. 2.5 mg, every morning. I give it to him myself.
Bisoprolol, 2.5 mg every morning. Any other long-term problems?
High blood pressure. Years and years.
Right. Do you have any allergies to medicines?
Oh dear. I think I came out in something once, years ago, after an antibiotic. But I can't remember which one, or what happened.
So a possible reaction to an antibiotic, but you're not sure which. We'll be careful, and I'll make a note.
Is that bad? Should I be frightened?
Not at all, it's simply a precaution. Now, you live on your own, I believe?
Yes, since my wife passed. The house is very quiet, you know.
I'm sorry. Dee comes twice a day, and that's a great help. Let me check your observations.
Blood pressure 108 over 64. Pulse 96. Temperature 36.9. Oxygen 97 percent. Breathing 16. And your weight is 58 kilos.
Is it very bad? Fifty-eight kilos is so low.
Those numbers are a little on the low side for blood pressure and a little fast for the pulse. Nothing frightening on its own.
Oh, thank goodness.
Open your mouth for me, please, and stick your tongue out.
Your mouth is rather dry. Now let me press your tummy. Tell me if it hurts.
Ooh, that's all right. Does it feel odd?
Your tummy is soft and not tender. That's a good sign.
What do you think it is, doctor? Is it cancer?
I understand why you ask. I don't want to guess about that today. What I think most likely is that you're mildly dehydrated because you've hardly been eating or drinking.
Mildly dehydrated. And that makes me tired?
It can. So we'll deal with it in steps. Today I'd like to order some blood tests, to check your kidneys, salts and blood count.
Can I take him down for those straight after?
Yes, please do. I'd also like to arrange a chest X-ray at the same time, since we're checking everything.
An X-ray too? Why the chest?
Because weight loss deserves a thorough look, and it's quick. It doesn't mean I've found anything.
All right. If you think it's best.
I do. In the meantime, Dee, small sips of fluid through the day, and little snacks rather than big plates.
I can do that. Soup, yoghurt, that sort of thing.
And a nice cup of tea, perhaps?
Tea counts. So, tests today, little and often with food and fluids. Does that make sense, Mr Okonkwo?
Yes. Tests today, little and often. Thank you for being kind, doctor.
Come on, Mr Okonkwo, I'll walk you down.

chief_complaint.value: I've not wanted any food and I've lost weight

physical_examination.finding: Your tummy is soft and not tender

clinical_actions.description: Small sips of fluid through the day and little snacks

clinical_uncertainties.description: Possible reaction to an unnamed antibiotic, reaction not remembered.
Neither patient nor carer can say when the weight loss began.
